title: Further Organic Chemistry and Spectroscopy
seo_title: Year 13 A Level Chemistry: Further Organic Chemistry Worksheets
standard_text: Optical isomerism, aldehydes and ketones, carboxylic acids and esters, acylation, aromatic chemistry, amines, polymers, amino acids, and analysis by mass spectrometry, infrared, NMR spectroscopy and chromatography.
meta_desc: Free Year 13 A level chemistry worksheets on further organic chemistry: naming esters, carbonyl tests, aromatic chemistry, polymers, mass spectra, infrared, ¹H NMR and chromatography. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: NMR: peaks = environments; n + 1 rule for splitting.
key_sub: Esters: alcohol part first (ethyl), acid part second (ethanoate).
body_html:
How to think about it

Esters are named alcohol part first, then acid part: ethanol + propanoic acid gives ethyl propanoate. Aldehydes give a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent; ketones do not. Benzene reacts by electrophilic substitution to keep its delocalised ring.

In ¹H NMR each hydrogen environment gives a peak, split into n + 1 lines by n hydrogens on the next carbon. The molecular ion in a mass spectrum is at Mr. Rf = spot distance ÷ solvent distance.

Example

Ester from ethanoic acid and propan-1-ol?

alcohol part: propyl

acid part: ethanoate

Answer: propyl ethanoate

Example

Splitting of the CH₃ peak in CH₃CH₂Cl?

2 H on the next carbon

2 + 1 = 3

Answer: triplet

Common mistakes

  • Naming the acid part of an ester first.
  • Counting the H atoms in the group itself for the n + 1 rule.
  • Thinking ketones give a silver mirror.

faq.q: What does the n + 1 rule say?
faq.a: A peak is split into n + 1 lines, where n is the number of hydrogens on the neighbouring carbon atoms.

faq.q: How do you tell an aldehyde from a ketone?
faq.a: Warm with Tollens' reagent: an aldehyde gives a silver mirror; a ketone does not react.

items.q: Which is the strongest base?

items.q: Why does benzene react by substitution rather than addition?

items.q: What is a racemic mixture?
